key_insight: DICE co-evolves fast student and teacher interatomic potentials, accelerating configuration exploration while limiting propagation of unreliable teacher labels.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a more efficient route to compact potentials for atomistic simulations of ceramics, solid electrolytes and metal–organic frameworks.
method: Use a fast student potential to explore configurations.
Assess representation-based support: route high-support configurations to teacher labelling and low-support configurations to DFT.
Alternate teacher and student updates rather than using fixed two-stage distillation.
evidence_signal: Across Al2O3, yttria-stabilised zirconia and MIL-120(Al), DICE used 140–494 target DFT reference configurations per system; recorded student exploration times were 2.6–5.1% of corresponding teacher-driven estimates.
watch_item: Reliability depends on support assessment correctly flagging configurations that need DFT; the reported timing comparison concerns exploration, not total workflow cost.
paper_title: Accelerating interatomic potential development through student-driven exploration and reliability-aware distillation
